"Maybe we could just stay here," one of them mutters, grinning and going back to the campfire. Maybe we could. "Do you recognize these mountains, …?," they ask. Another day. It's been so long, I hardly ever recognize myself. Maybe we could just stay here."

options.name: A terrible shame.

events.title: Failed Expedition

events.desc: The expedition members come across a river that is bursting at the banks. They can try to raft across, which would be quick, but dangerous. Alternatively, they could search for a more suitable place to cross, though this could take some time.
events.flavor: "A brief landscape captured in the moment that found us. The bold grays, the prospective river trapped in a cage of violence and impetus. These wandering trees, carried away, decapitated. Sometimes, some type of animal. Otherwise, alone."

options.name: Onward!
Better to be safe.
Jump! Jump! Jump!

events.title: Swollen River

events.desc: The expedition successfully crossed the river, with little to no difficulty.
events.flavor:
"With such an easy crossing, we will make great strides today. Why, I dare say we could have made many more if we loaded the rafts that bit more."

"Are you touched in the head, son? We're lucky the waters opted to be gentle today. Let's get the rafts out before the waters stop being so kind."

options.name: Good news.

events.title: Safe Crossing

events.desc: Unfortunately the expedition's raft capsized while crossing the river and several supplies were lost.
events.flavor: "The water was too fast, we only just made it to the other bank. And we were the lucky ones. Once the other raft went under the waters, the last thing I saw of my brother was the rapids swallowing his hand."

options.name: Unfortunate.

events.title: Capsized Raft

events.desc: A large grizzly has been sighted up ahead. We could hang back and wait for it to leave or we could hunt it.
events.flavor:
"Here the bears grow lean and famished. That does not make it any better; the keen eyes, the craving jaws, the drops of saliva dripping down the yellowed fangs. They're always so alert here. So vigilant.

Oh, but it isn't only for them that food is scarce around these mountains."

options.name: We shall hunt it.
Better to be safe.

events.title: Bear Sighted

events.desc: The expedition has successfully hunted and killed the grizzly bear.
events.flavor: "We stalked it carefully, but relentlessly. A few good shots were enough to put it down. It's times like this where I wish my manservant weren't as good a shot as he is. I could have used a trophy like that for my boudoir."

options.name: Failure would have been unbearable.

events.title: Successful Bear Hunt

events.desc: The expedition attempted to hunt the bear but it went wrong.
events.flavor: "The hunt started off well enough, but too late we realized it was a mother bear with her cubs. It's a fact well appreciated that you never come between a mother bear and her cubs."

options.name: Onward!

events.title: Bear Hunt Failure

events.desc: The grizzly bear that was earlier ignored, attacks the expedition.
events.flavor: "It came hurtling out of the woods faster than a speeding …. Roaring like nothing you've ever heard. It took several volleys to take it down and that was only after we'd lost two of our own."

options.name: Damn shame.

events.title: Bear Attacks

events.desc: A member of the expedition wishes to stop for a day or so and take some wildlife photographs.
events.flavor: "The buffalo kept their heads down, grazing peacefully. Unbothered, their grizzled bodies moved around the sea of grass, bigger than the ones in Europe. Even from a distance we could see the mazes that rabbits and foxes had dug close to them, and the scarce trees danced with the grace of a young debutante."

options.name: Great idea.
There is no time for this.

events.title: Wildlife Photography

events.desc: A member of the expedition has suggested we detour to climb a mountain and claim it in the name of ….
events.flavor: "One of the expedition members has his eyes locked on the mountain. "It's a good risk, my friend," he says, "I don't think anyone has claimed this one yet, you see, imagine how they'd pay us back home—all for this insignificant rock." Snow slides down the mountainside, melted like threads of gray cotton."

options.name: Excellent idea
We can't spare the time.

events.title: Mountain Sighted

events.desc: Upon arriving at the summit of the mountain you see it already had been claimed by ….
events.flavor:
"We should have known we wouldn't be the first here."

"I sense a running theme with you lot. You and yours go west, thinking you've found something spectacular, only to find out someone else got there first."

"If this is another lecture about history repeating itself, I'll send you up to claim the mountain. Alone. With a bent fork. We haven't tried that before now, have we?"

options.name: Unfortunate.

events.title: Mountain Already Claimed

events.desc: The expedition has scaled the mountain and claimed it in the name of …. They have also decided to name it 'Mount …'.
events.flavor: With one, final heave, … threw … over the lip of the last cliff. As … straightened both posture and snowy clothes, the first light of a new day broke behind them. A hero's welcome to the west, and a mountain claimed. And the cream on top of the mash, the flag of …, brought forth by a younger expeditionary.

options.name: Excellent.

events.title: Mountain Claimed

events.desc: While climbing the mountain, a rockfall struck a member of the expedition, rendering them unconscious. The group was forced to turn back.
events.flavor: As the rocks tumbled down the mountain, snow cascading in their wake, blood dripped over the ledge where a struck expeditionary lay. The steam escaping his split lips were the only sign of life from the poor boy. With a pang of guilt, … threw the boy over … shoulders and marched down the mountain.

options.name: A shame.

events.title: Mountainside Issues

events.desc: Some members of the expedition have expressed concern that the weather is turning against them. They insist on hunkering down to avoid the worst of it.
events.flavor: "The layers of snow kept growing like untreated tumors. A huge white, a great white, and the reflection of it making our eyes sore and hurt. If we don't stop now, maybe we won't be able to stop anymore. One of the men shivers as he rubs his arms—lips as pale as our shadow over the snow. He doesn't say a word."

options.name: Press on.
Heed their warning.

events.title: Snow on the Ground

events.desc: While it was difficult, the expedition has successfully pushed through the snow.
events.flavor: "We had to move double time, and no doubt it wasn't pleasant but, finally we're through the worst of it."

options.name: Good.

events.title: Survived the Snow

events.desc: Unfortunately the expedition got caught in a snow storm, a few members died and several supplies were lost.
events.flavor: "Poor visibility, biting cold and on top of it all the gnawing feeling that I had made an error of judgment."

options.name: Unfortunate.

events.title: Lost in the Snow

events.desc: After a while the snow has subsided enough to push on.
events.flavor: "It is a good thing we didn't try to go out in that. It would have been a disaster."

options.name: Great news.

events.title: Snow Clears

events.desc: A member of the expedition has asked for a few days to stop and collect samples of a previously unknown plant species.

options.name: Of course.
What are we, gardeners?!

events.title: Undiscovered Plant Species

events.desc: The expedition to map the west has been traveling in circles. … can either pick a random direction and push on, or wait for night to fall and use the stars as a guide.

options.name: Push on.
Wait for nightfall.

events.title: A Circular Expedition

events.desc: The members of the expedition managed to get even more lost. Eventually they found the right way but not before wasting a large amount of supplies and time.
events.flavor: "We struck out in a random direction and it did not pay off."

options.name: How irksome.

events.title: Hopelessly Lost

events.desc: The expedition managed to find the correct trail again and have set off, losing relatively little time.
events.flavor: "We picked a direction, almost at random. Good thing it turned out to be the right one."

options.name: Great News

events.title: Back on Track

events.flavor:
"It was an unusually cold month when the range of mountains announced their unmerciful judgement before us. As the sun started to set, a glistening light penetrated the canopy of trees, making the shadows tremble and the raindrops cover the brown, almost dead grass.

Our expedition was tired, and that tiredness of the soul—far from home and close to the ocean—became much more tangible when the last rays illuminated their swollen faces."

options.name: The perfect place to build a fort.
We cannot afford this delay.
We shall stop and rest.

events.title: A Stop on the Way

events.desc: The expedition is waken up in the middle of the night. Inhuman screams come from one of the tents, and a female voice cries: "Baby!".

options.name: We will take care of the baby.
It's best for both of them to go back to a village.

events.title: The Miracle of Life

events.flavor: "But we... you know, captain, it's been a while since we are far from home and... hic! Explorers will be explorers, right? We were just exploring a bit... in some other direction, hic! But exploring nonetheless!"

options.name: These men need some discipline.
They just needed a break.

events.title: An Explorer's Life for Me

events.flavor:
"Document the new species of plants and flowers, draw them, draw the animals, document them too. One of our men has the hand and talent of an artist, although his difficulties with the anatomy have already been questioned by a few members. Regardless, he's been of great help during this expedition.

Most of the others are sent hunting as our journey leaves behind the mapped villages and roads that others followed before us. It is just us, now, us and the wild."

options.name: Hunting must be prioritized.
It's imperative that we find a settlement.

events.title: A New Quest

events.flavor:
"As days come and go, our landscape offers minimal changes. These mountains are sharper, these are older, more eroded; now the river runs on this side, now it runs on the other side, but the chain of circumstances stays the same.

Our men came back with great news and announced that another native settlement was found, so we prepared our gifts: needles, and mirrors, and medals, and ribbons, and all accessories that looked rich and beautiful. We had already repeated the ritual a hundred times, but every one felt equally important—we needed their help."

options.name: We should try to barter with them.
Is there anyone here who can guide us?
They have offered us some provisions for the baby and its mother.

events.title: Peaceful Intentions

events.desc: The expedition men who had been sent hunting have found an area by the riverbank, filled with every animal that they had encountered during their travel. The question is: which one to hunt?
events.flavor: "The forest was a dream of greenness and bears, wild boars, wolves, deer and bison, hare, foxes and even goats. It was filled with their sounds and movement, like a living book. Nature ran free and unscathed, and the feeling of letting oneself lose was a significant temptation, back to the gardens of paradise."

options.name: We cannot afford any risks. Go for a small animal.
We need the food. Go for the big game.

events.title: Hunting

events.flavor: "At the mauvish beginnings of dawn, the shadows of the mountains become lilac imprints, carvings on the rocks that mimic their own figures as miniatures displayed in a museum. The gorge gets sharper and narrower, the mouth of the Earth directly pointed at us—some hungers you cannot satiate."

options.name: Our guide knows better.
We have no time to waste.
She knows these paths.

events.title: When the Earth Opened Its Mouth

events.desc: The expedition finds a small hut in the mountains. Half-ruined, it appears to have been used by Spanish missionaries and is now empty.
events.flavor:
"This is the perfect place for a mutiny. A riot. I've put these men through arduous perils, that they won't forget. I saw two of them talking earlier today. They muttered among themselves and gazed in my direction only occasionally, proving that their intentions weren't as noble as they seemed.

I can feel their eager eyes upon me now. How they looked at the cabin and nodded at each other, "we should stay the night here, sir." Of course they'd say so."

options.name: We still need to stay the night somewhere.
We can't give them this opportunity.

events.title: Cabin Fever

events.desc: After a long and arduous journey, the expedition has finally come to an end. The most interesting discovery of the journey, was that the long fabled Buenaventura river does not actually exist!
events.flavor:
"A disappointment. And a tough one. We revised the maps over and over, checked with the locals, followed the marks, the maps - again. How is it possible for a river to not exist? For it to have so many witnesses and still not be?

What did the Franciscan missionaries see, then? A lake, perhaps. Another river. There is a sense of defeat that comes to a man with such a force that makes mountains tremble and the mind shiver. "Nothing," the man next to me says, his eyes hurting with an impassive decency, "we found nothing.""

options.name: A disappointment, but an educational one.

events.title: Buenaventura River

events.desc: After a long and arduous journey, the expedition has finally come to an end. The expedition has managed to map the entire length of the Oregon Trail.
events.flavor:
"A newly drawn map has been laid out on the back of a wooden wagon. The ink blinks, still wet, and its shining curves follow the just discovered trails as tributaries of a river.

A young boy comes bearing a cup of tea; quiet, demure, curious. He tries to take a look at the map, but his education stops him. He leaves the tea on the table and walks away quietly. "His dad got lost in these mountains," another member says, "good thing we got them all mapped now.""

options.name: Wonderful news.

events.title: Oregon Trail

events.desc: After a long and arduous journey, the expedition has finally come to an end. The expedition has managed to find and map the entirety of the Great Salt Lake
events.flavor: "I will always remember our reflection in the water. How the triumphant silhouette of the expedition was painted there like an oil canvas. The colors, all mixed together and, somehow, so pungent. Faces floated in the lake with unrecognizable features. It was us. It could have been anyone else. Ah, but it was us."

options.name: Wonderful news!

events.title: The Great Salt Lake

events.desc: Finding both the … public and supposed political allies unreceptive to … ideas, frustrated, … has decided to retire from the realm of politics, opting instead to spend the rest of … days penning embittered reflections on what could have been.
events.flavor:
"I give these bumpkins the truth, and how am I rewarded?
With deafening silence!
And they call … a city of ideas? Of culture?
The only evidence of cultivation I've found in that cesspool of a city came from the fields outside of it, and even they were cared for poorly.
Good riddance to you all I say, sirs!
Good riddance to you all!"

options.name: Let … peddle … ideas in peace, away from ….
Politely inform … … presence is unwanted in ….
The … just needs a little "nudge" to get … back in the game.

events.title: Infertile Grounds

events.desc: Satisfied with the state of politics in …, and eyeing new opportunities for agitation abroad, … has declared … intentions to leave the country—wishing its current custodians the best of luck in the years to come.
events.flavor:
"Friends, what we have achieved here in … is nothing less than astounding. The … cause is …'s cause, and our labors and our results serves as proof of just that.

But in the celebration of our fortunes, we should not forget those abroad, whose … aspirations are still but a faint hope, struggling under the boots of our enemies.

As long as their cause remains, so does mine. I cannot in good conscience rest on my laurels in …, ignoring their cries for justice."

options.name: Fare well, …. May your ideas find ready ears abroad.

events.title: To Greener Grounds

events.desc: Content with the new state of affairs in …, and unwilling or unable to face the uncertainties that life abroad offers, … has officially announced … retirement from political life.
events.flavor:
"So now …'s off. To … if the rumors are true—to paint, drink, and raise chickens. Seems that herding men gives one a taste for herding …'s simpler creatures too."

"Maybe … just likes chickens, …?"

"Shut your bloody mouth, …."

options.name: Even firebrands cool off in the end it would seem.
Let us honor … memory. A bust in … perhaps?

events.title: The Fruits of Thy Labor

events.desc: With recent developments, the … government has taken an interest in pursuing the mission of unifying the South Slavic peoples.
events.flavor:
The … stands before the people of … to deliver an impassioned speech.

"It is inevitable that we pursue the formation and development of a Yugoslavia that unites all South Slavic peoples. … can most certainly lead the effort."

options.name: Our … will lead this effort.
There is too much disharmony to pursue this plot.

events.title: A Case for Yugoslavia

events.desc: Through the great efforts of … …, … is an established nation unifying … and other South Slavic peoples.
events.flavor: With the dream of … realized, … … stands prepared to lead the nation into a new era of prosperity and prestige.

options.name: The future of … is bright.

events.title: The Unifier of South Slavic Peoples

events.desc: While … has succeeded to power in Oman and Muscat, his younger brother … has established an independent powerbase as the … of … in East Africa.
events.flavor: "Why Africa? Look around you! The waters around Zanzibar are a more brilliant blue than the sky itself, the white sands are so fine that I could rest on the shore and imagine I was upon a hundred cushions, and all the goods of Africa you can imagine can be had in its markets. Why struggle in Oman when I can build an empire here with these riches?"

options.name: … still reigns supreme!
Our fortunes lie with ….
Stop …! … cannot be divided.

events.title: The Rise of Zanzibar

events.desc: Some enterprising explorers and merchants aligned with colonial interests are claiming that it would be trivial to undercut … authority in Africa by directly obtaining treaties with local chieftains in the region. By all accounts, …'s authority is extremely weak—letting this happen will lead to us gaining … and the overnight collapse of … entirely.
events.flavor:
"I'm telling you, that man is half-crazy! That whole scheme of his will founder the moment we let go of his hand!"

Cigar smoke wafted in the dim light of the drawing room, as the two figures silently considered what to do. "Perhaps," pondered the other voice, "that just means we musn't let go of his hand." There was a slight pause, interrupted by a chuckle. "The Zanj is lovely in the spring, I've been told."

options.name: We can gain much from the end of ….
We gain nothing from ruining ….

events.title: The … East Africa Company

events.desc: Colonial officials from … have circumvented our outposts and obtained agreements with inland chiefs we have long claimed are under our rule. Our illusions of East African supremacy have collapsed overnight with this act, and local warlords and other colonial powers are rapidly dismantling what remains of our empire.
events.flavor: The sharp beat of … boots marching through … woke up the entire city. A growing crowd followed them as the soldiers proceeded to the main square, and gasped as they raised the flag of …. Who were these people? Where was the …? What was happening to …?

options.name: This is …'s darkest hour.

events.title: The Lion With No Pride

events.desc: Through deft diplomacy and studious statecraft, we have secured control of the Zanj. Today, … stands tall!
events.flavor: A new pamphlet was making the rounds among the coffeehouses and booksellers of …: The True Chronicles of Zanzibar. A folk history, it spoke of Unguja Island's glorious origins under the leadership of Queen Aziza, a mythical figure once almost completely forgotten. Like Aziza, Zanzibar itself had now climbed back from the shadows, reclaiming a place for itself in the spotlight, and that light could be seen on every beaming Zanzibari face as they read of their glorious past and dreamed of their glorious future.

options.name: A glorious day for us all!

events.title: Heirs of Queen Aziza

events.desc: An ambitious slave and ivory merchant named Hamad ibn Muhammad al Murjabi asks for …'s support in a colonial venture. He proposes establishing a new government in Lualaba. If he is supported, his state will become our subject, but the great powers will disapprove and set our quest to become Recognized back considerably.
events.flavor:
"Why do they call you 'Tippu Tip' anyways, Hamad?" asked the foreigner as the ivory caravan began to ford another river.

The trader smiled. "It is because of the sound of my guns, for you see—oh, blast, look!"

He bolted towards the water, calling for help from his caravan.

"The boat full of slaves has sunk!" he cried. "What a pity! That was a fine canoe."

options.name: Tippu Tip cannot be supported, but we dare not condemn him.
We welcome this foothold in the Congo.
Restrain Tippu Tip and end this before it can begin!
Convince Tippu Tip he can better further his interests here, with us.

events.title: Tippu Tip

events.desc: The rise of …, a notable … figure, marks the end of centuries of Arab rule. … leaders are demanding that this monumental occasion be used to officially overturn … dominance within ….
events.flavor:
The streets of Zanzibar's old Stone Town quarter were deserted. Everyone had shuttered themselves in their homes, waiting to see what tomorrow would bring.

Initially, some had celebrated, and claimed that while a hundred tribes had lost their freedom centuries ago, a nation had regained theirs today. Others had looked out onto the island of white sands and blue waters and feared that if they did nothing today, they would lose everything tomorrow. They had all poured out into the streets, briefly, and soon ran into each other.

Too many people had become abruptly aware that their neighbors were strangers to them, and so now they waited alone, side by side.

options.name: … belongs to the … nation!
One … … is irrelevant—… remains ….

events.title: The End of Arab Rule?
